notes: RULED BLOCKED by the coordinator (2026-11-26): the REST-API copy is not accepted after a bot check on the web pages. For the human's hand fetch: the reader reported that the copy gave 290–425 mm TL (n = 18, mean 352), not the paper's 352–379, and confirmed peak reaction 0.84–1.08 m and 0.26 per attack / 0.11 per reaction — verify when fetched. Previous reading notes: The reaction distances and capture success check. The size range does not. Other values: the Michaelis–Menten fit of smallmouth peak reaction distance to light gave Rmax = 101.5 cm (R² = 0.71); a parabolic fit on log10 light gave R² = 0.90 (a = −434.33, b = 78.13, c = −2.85). Burbot's maximum reaction distance was 98 cm, with 5.0 % success. Smallmouth had a dark (lateral-line) detection radius of 40 cm, 11.2 % of TL (p. 39). Smallmouth attacked mottled sculpin about twice as often as round goby. Claims as first recorded: adult smallmouth reacted at 0.84–1.08 m at peak [source as read: mean peak reaction distances (n = 12 per light level): civil twilight CT-4 100.0 cm, sunrise 108.2 cm, midmorning 84.1 cm; lower at CT-6 (67.5 cm) and in the dark (40.1 cm). The longest single reaction was 159 cm (sunrise)] | smallmouth of 352–379 mm [source as read: smallmouth bass 290–425 mm TL (n = 18); mean 352 mm TL] | smallmouth capture success on round goby and mottled sculpin of 0.26 per attack (0.11 per reaction), in the laboratory under dim to bright light [source as read: 630 attacks with 26 % retained (164 prey: 61 round goby, 103 mottled sculpin); 1,510 reactions, a 10.9 % success rate overall]
